items.title: Weekly improvement cycle ({label}): {name} — readouts, rules & generators, next experiments
items.body:
Weekly recursive self-improvement (RSI) cycle for {name} ({label}, repo `{repo_name}`), driven automatically by the channel registry (Ben, 20 Nov 2026; J3257; docs/RSI_LOOP.md). Replaces the old monthly-improvement review.

1) INGEST AUTOPSIES: run `python3 scripts/rsi.py ingest-autopsies --channel {slug} --apply` to turn every new J3256 retention autopsy (`05_Analytics/{slug}/autopsy/<video_id>_<48h|7d>.md`) into deduplicated candidate experiments (live-video packaging fixes -> Test & Compare; next-film production fixes -> next N films).
2) READ DUE EXPERIMENTS: run `python3 scripts/rsi.py cycle --channel {slug}` and evaluate every running experiment whose readout_date is due against recorded snapshots, Studio reads, first-day checks, and autopsies:
   - PASS (only when observed sample >= min_sample, with evidence and a revert_plan): record with `python3 scripts/rsi.py record <id> --result pass --sample <n> --evidence "..." --changelog "..."`; promote the proven rule to `05_Analytics/LEARNINGS.md` and {name}'s own repo (`{repo_name}`) `studio/RULES.md`, playbook, AND update the actual generators agents use (script template, title shapes & scorer, thumbnail checks, picture-plan template, prompts).
   - FAIL: record `--result fail`, revert the change, and record why.
   - INCONCLUSIVE: record `--result inconclusive` (extends readout_date once by 14 days; a second inconclusive readout drops it).
3) START NEXT EXPERIMENTS: fill open slots up to the cap of 3 live experiments for {label} from the highest-impact guardrailed candidates (`python3 scripts/rsi.py start <id>`).
4) VALIDATE & DELIVER: run `python3 scripts/rsi.py validate`. Open ONE PR per repo touched (`{repo_name}` for channel rules/generators; studio repo for `05_Analytics/EXPERIMENTS.json` and `05_Analytics/LEARNINGS.md`) for the Chief, with one changelog line per change.

Guards: £0. Read-only on live videos except allowed Test & Compare listing tests. Never change Ben's gates, the never-list, money/billing, or a channel's direction (e.g. Rule 34 item 7, Ben's plans) — escalate those to Ben in one line instead. Never promote a rule on fewer than min_sample. End parked for Chief review (`jobs.py block <id> --reason "parked for Chief: weekly improvement cycle ({label}) PRs ready" --git`).
items.remaining_action: Run weekly improvement cycle for {name}

items.body: Weekly growth audit for Orbit With Ben (aim: numbers up month on month). 0) First-day checks (Ben, 10 Nov 2026): start from `python3 scripts/launch_check.py report`. It lists every video checked six hours after it went live, its verdict, and what the weak starts share. A difference shared by three weak starts goes into this audit as a proposed rule or test for 05_Analytics/LEARNINGS.md, with the video ids; a weak start whose `Done` line is empty is named for the Chief. 1) Pull last 28 days and last 7 days from YouTube Analytics with the read-only tracker sign-in (YT_ANALYTICS_REFRESH_TOKEN_OWB; 05_Analytics tools): views, impressions CTR, AVD/retention curves, subs per video, Shorts vs longs, traffic sources, search terms. 2) What's working and what isn't: top/bottom 3 by CTR and retention, with the frame or title that explains it. 3) Competitors: 5 reference channels (Astrum, History of the Universe, SEA, Kurzgesagt, melodysheep) last 30 days via public pages/yt-dlp metadata only: titles, thumbs, lengths, view velocity, topics trending. 4) Write 05_Analytics/weekly_audit/OWB_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md: findings, then 3-5 concrete changes for the next films in production (title/thumb/opening/length/topic), each tied to a film id, plus 3 new video ideas ranked by evidence. Compare with last week's file and say what moved. 4b) Shorts lab (Ben, 21 Oct 2026, from Gemini's read of the HOS gold Short: 44% viewed on 25 s, the feed stopped after the first pool): for every Short public 48 h or more and not yet in the table, add one row to the Shorts lab table in 05_Analytics/LEARNINGS.md: id, title, length (s), views, stayed-to-watch % (Studio's Viewed vs swiped away; from the daily Studio read, studio_ctr.json), average % viewed, the second where the retention curve (Analytics API audienceWatchRatio by elapsedVideoTimeRatio) falls most, and what is on screen and said at that second (from the Short's cut list and VO words). Targets: stayed-to-watch 60%+ (Ben's floor, 24 Oct; 70%+ stretch), average viewed 70%+ (Ben's second floor, 24 Oct 20:03; aim 100%+ = rewatches via loop endings). 4d) Two-target check (Ben, 24 Oct 2026; orbit-build-shorts.mdc → '60% stayed-to-watch' and '70% average viewed'): also grade average viewed LOOP ≥100 / PASS ≥70 / WATCH 50–69.9 / MISS <50 with runtime, longest plate hold, payoff time and whether the last line loops into line 1; for every Short with a 48 h+ Studio read in the last 14 days, list stayed-to-watch % against the 60% target as PASS (≥60), WATCH (45–59.9), MISS (<45) or too few (<100 Studio views), plus the frame-0 source (video, or a still and its zoom), the first-word onset, the first cut (s) and whether a meta-promise is present. Say which of the six 60% rules the misses break, and propose re-cuts only for Shorts not yet public (local renders only; any swap goes to Ben). 4c) Learnings: turn this week's evidence into at most 3 rules or tests in the Learnings table of LEARNINGS.md (rule, evidence with ids and numbers, status: test/proven/dropped). A rule proven on 3+ Shorts is proposed to the Chief for the Shorts brief and the playbook; a test names the next 2-4 Shorts it runs on. Keep the audit itself to one page: what moved, the lab rows, the rules. Spend nothing: existing subscriptions and free tools only, no paid API, no TTS or picture generation in these growth jobs (credits are for pipeline VO and picture; floors are 0, Ben 12 Oct 14:46), no Studio or publish change. End with jobs.py block <id> --reason "parked for Chief: <what to decide>" --git.

items.title: Weekly OWB thumbnail audit: every long + Short thumb vs style, CTR and competitors -> new Test & Compare Bs for the weakest
items.body:
Weekly thumbnail audit for Orbit With Ben (Ben, 28 Oct 2026: "audit all the video thumbnails ... check that they match our style, that they perform well, and let's iterate and improve them ... at a higher click-through rate. A full audit every week ... generate new thumbnails if we need to, and add the thumbnails onto the shorts, the longs"). GBP0 beyond the plans; no Replace, no delete.

1. **Inventory.** Every public and scheduled Orbit With Ben video, longs and Shorts: id, title, publish date, the live thumbnail (save a copy), and whether a Test & Compare is running (05_Analytics/tests/THUMB_LEDGER.json).
2. **Style.** Score every long thumb against 00_Brand/Channel-Setup/THUMBNAIL_AND_TITLE_RULES.md (and AGENTS.md 'Long thumbnails' for OWB: saturation, near-black, lit subject, band rule): PASS/FAIL with the rule broken. Make a 168 px sheet with `00_Brand/Channel-Setup/tools/thumb_preview.py` and judge readability at that size. Shorts: score the cover/frame 0 against the Shorts rules (one question, readable hook).
3. **Performance.** From YouTube Analytics (read-only tracker sign-in), last 28 days per video: impressions, impressions CTR, views from impressions; channel median CTR for longs and for Shorts separately. Flag the bottom quarter by CTR (only videos with 1,000+ impressions) and every style FAIL. Read back any Test & Compare that has finished (`scripts/thumb_ledger.py result`).

**Competitor study (Ben, 28 Oct 2026: "other channels audit our competitors all the time, see what they're doing for their thumbnails, and try to match what works well for them, including the titles. Let's try to iterate all the time, constantly improve and perfect these channels").** Run it before step 4 every week:
- Channels: Astrum, History of the Universe, SEA, Kurzgesagt, melodysheep (plus any space channel outranking us on our own titles in YouTube search). Public pages / yt-dlp metadata and thumbnail images only.
- For each, the last 90 days: the 10 fastest and 10 slowest videos by views per day since publish, longs and Shorts separately. Save the thumbnails and titles.
- Code each one: words on the thumb, text size/colour, subject (object, face, scene), contrast and darkness, composition, curiosity gap; title shape (question / number / 'What happens if' / statement), length, the hook word.
- Find the patterns the fast videos share and the slow ones don't, and compare them with our own thumbs and titles.
- Use the strongest patterns in this week's Bs. For the 3 weakest videos also write a title B and run a title Test & Compare where Studio allows it (one variable per test: thumbnail or title, not both at once).
- Keep the running record in `05_Analytics/weekly_thumb_audit/PATTERNS.md`: each pattern tried, where, and its result from the ledger. Patterns that win twice go into the channel's THUMBNAIL_AND_TITLE_RULES.md via the Chief; ones that lose twice are dropped. Decide from the data; nothing goes to Ben.
4. **Improve.** For the 3 weakest longs without a running test (lowest CTR first, then style FAILs): design a new B in the house builders (Codex designs, kind thumb; existing plates or master frames first; any image generation only inside the plan, never paid extra). Checks: 1280x720, under 2 MB, readable at 168 px, nothing under the duration badge, no Orbit on long thumbs (OWB). Run `scripts/packaging_panel.py` for the three independent critiques and apply what they agree on. Then queue one Studio job per B to arm Test & Compare (A = live, B = new; never just swap the live thumb), and `thumb_ledger.py add`/`start` it.
   Shorts: where Studio lets a Short take a chosen cover, queue a Studio job to set the best frame or our cover; where it doesn't, note it and feed the finding into the next Shorts' frame 0 instead.
5. **Report** `05_Analytics/weekly_thumb_audit/OWB/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`: the inventory table (thumb, style PASS/FAIL, CTR vs median, test status), what changed since last week's file and which tests moved CTR, the new Bs with their sheets, and 3 lessons for next week's designs (add any that hold up to the rules file through the Chief). Park for Chief; the Chief passes the new Bs before their Studio jobs run.

items.title: Weekly search research (Orbit + Field Order History): vidIQ demand, Anglosphere adult value, top-10 gap, small-channel outliers
items.body:
Weekly search-led topic research for Orbit With Ben and Field Order History (Ben OK, 20 Nov 2026; J3222; STUDIO_PLAYBOOK.md §2, LEARNINGS.md rule 37, ww2-channel 00_Brand/PLAYBOOK.md §7). Runs in a Claude cloud lane (`needs: cloud`) because vidIQ only works in a Claude lane. Budget: up to 100 vidIQ credits for Orbit and up to 50 vidIQ credits for Field Order History per run (£0 beyond existing subscriptions; never buy credits, top up, or exceed the budget). First run by 7 Dec 2026 so January's ranked list is ready before the 30 Dec format-test readout.

1) ORBIT WITH BEN (up to 100 vidIQ credits; effective for topics locked from 1 Jan 2027). Run steps 1-4 weekly and step 8 monthly (first run of each month):
- Step 1 DEMAND: ~50 Orbit space subjects (planets, moons, missions, telescopes, sky events, mysteries, calm/sleep documentaries). For each: vidIQ keyword research (monthly searches, competition, growth, top countries); signed-out YouTube autocomplete with the US locale for exact phrasing; Google Trends for seasonality. Keep 10k-150k searches/month at competition 45 or under.
- Step 2 VALUE: Anglosphere (US, UK, Canada, Australia among top markets; not dominated by low-paying markets), adult intent (no kids or made-for-kids queries), evergreen, able to carry a 10-20 minute long and a series, plus an earnings/RPM proxy from vidIQ estimates for sub-niche channels.
- Step 3 RESULTS-PAGE GAP: signed-out top 10 (vidIQ youtube_search or signed-out YouTube) — video age, views, channel size, and whether each actually answers the query. Score the gap as the count of old (3+ years), weak, off-target or small-channel results.
- Step 4 SMALL-CHANNEL PROOF: vidIQ outliers — last-12-month videos on the subject from channels under 50k subscribers at 5x or more of their channel's usual views. None found means no real opening.
- Step 8 OUR OWN SEARCH TERMS (monthly): read YouTube Analytics' search terms for Orbit With Ben. Double down on clusters whose search views grow, and flag any cluster to drop after about three films below the bar.
Write `05_Analytics/owb/search_research/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`: the ranked table (query, volume, competition, top countries, adult, RPM proxy, top-10 gap, small-channel outliers, cluster) plus the top three film ideas with search-led titles (query words + one hook, 3 title candidates + 2 thumb ideas sketched against outliers), each tagged with its cluster and the format it fits.

2) FIELD ORDER HISTORY / WW2 (up to 50 vidIQ credits; for the next topics after film 010). Run steps 1-4 for candidate WW2 topics beyond film 010: search demand for the topic's own phrasing, English-speaking (US/UK/CA/AU) adult audience, signed-out top-10 results-page gap, and small-channel (<50k subs, 5x+) outliers. Write `05_Analytics/ww2/search_research/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`: the ranked table plus the top candidate topics for film 011+.

Guards: no change to December's films, schedule or format tests; do not lock, script or build any new Orbit long before December's readouts (Rule 34); no TTS, picture generation, or Studio/publish changes. Finish with `jobs.py done <id> --result "wrote owb + ww2 search_research/<date>.md; Orbit top 3: ...; WW2 top 3: ...; credits used: <owb>/100 + <ww2>/50" --git`.
